content.title: About
content.content: Popcorn is an airy grain snack made by heating whole corn kernels until they burst. In movie theaters it is commonly served with melted butter, giving it a distinctive aroma and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popcorn is the only type of corn that “pops” due to its high internal moisture content.
The first commercial popcorn was sold in the United States in 1885.
Americans consume more than 15 million tons of popcorn each year.
Theater popcorn is often served in large portions, and adding butter almost doubles its calorie count.
There are over 30 popcorn flavors, but classic butter remains the most popular.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Unlike many sweet snacks, popcorn contains very little sugar, making it easier to manage blood glucose levels.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Popcorn is rich in dietary fiber, which supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Polysaccharides and polyphenols in popcorn help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low fat content (without butter)
items.content: Plain popcorn is virtually fat‑free; adding butter increases fat, but using a quality oil can provide healthier fats.

items.title: Heart‑friendly
items.content: Fiber and antioxidants contribute to lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: High calories with butter
items.content: Melted butter significantly raises the calorie and saturated fat content.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Commercial theater popcorn often contains salt and preservatives, which may be undesirable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Large pieces can pose a choking risk for young children.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy should choose a butter‑free version.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Popcorn can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, at the movies, mixed with nuts, dried fruit, or spices. When served with butter, drizzle melted butter evenly over the popcorn and toss gently.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store popcorn in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. If butter is added, consume within a few days to keep it crisp, as it can become soggy over time.
